Which of the following best describes liquidity?

the amount by which government revenue exceeds government spending in a period
items.s: liquidity: the ease with which an asset can be converted into money without loss. The other options describe budget surplus, marginal cost, gross domestic product.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines international trade?
o: the difference between income earned abroad and income paid abroad
a policy that increases aggregate demand through higher spending or lower taxes
the amount by which quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied at a price
the exchange of goods and services between one country and another
items.s: international trade: the exchange of goods and services between one country and another. The other options describe excess demand, expansionary policy, net factor income from abroad.

items.q: Which of the following best describes budget deficit?
o: the amount by which government spending exceeds government revenue in a period
the use of government spending and taxation to influence the economy
the fall in average cost that comes with a larger scale of production
the quantity of a good producers are willing to offer at each price
items.s: budget deficit: the amount by which government spending exceeds government revenue in a period. The other options describe fiscal policy, economies of scale, supply.

items.q: Which of the following best describes contribution?
o: the excess of price over average variable cost for each unit sold
the responsiveness of demand for one good to a change in the price of another
a change in supply caused by a factor other than the price of the good
the situation of people who are willing and able to work but have no job
items.s: contribution: the excess of price over average variable cost for each unit sold. The other options describe shift in supply, cross elasticity of demand, unemployment.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines fixed cost.
o: the situation of people who are willing and able to work but have no job
a cost that does not change with the level of output in the short run
a sustained rise in the general price level of goods and services
improvement in income living standards and economic structure of a country
items.s: fixed cost: a cost that does not change with the level of output in the short run. The other options describe inflation, unemployment, economic development.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines foreign direct investment.
o: a change in supply caused by a factor other than the price of the good
a policy that reduces aggregate demand through lower spending or higher taxes
a deliberate reduction in the official value of a country currency in terms of other currencies
investment by a firm in productive assets located in another country
items.s: foreign direct investment: investment by a firm in productive assets located in another country. The other options describe shift in supply, devaluation, contractionary policy.

items.q: The statement “the income households have left after paying direct taxes” describes which of the following?
o: net national product
gross domestic product
depreciation
disposable income
items.s: disposable income is the income households have left after paying direct taxes.

items.q: disinflation may be defined as
o: improvement in income living standards and economic structure of a country
a fall in the rate of inflation without a fall in the price level
the situation of people who are willing and able to work but have no job
the responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in the price of the good
items.s: disinflation: a fall in the rate of inflation without a fall in the price level. The other options describe price elasticity of demand, unemployment, economic development.

items.q: central bank may be defined as
o: the institution that issues currency and regulates the banking system
the amount by which quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded at a price
a measure of the average price of a fixed basket of consumer goods
the price at which quantity demanded equals quantity supplied
items.s: central bank: the institution that issues currency and regulates the banking system. The other options describe consumer price index, excess supply, equilibrium price.

items.q: Which of the following best describes income elasticity of demand?
o: the buying and selling of government securities by the central bank
the quantity bought and sold when the market is in equilibrium
the responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in household income
gross domestic product plus net factor income from abroad
items.s: income elasticity of demand: the responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in household income. The other options describe equilibrium quantity, open market operation, gross national product.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines unemployment.
o: a measure of the average price of a fixed basket of consumer goods
the responsiveness of demand for one good to a change in the price of another
a cost that does not change with the level of output in the short run
the situation of people who are willing and able to work but have no job
items.s: unemployment: the situation of people who are willing and able to work but have no job. The other options describe fixed cost, cross elasticity of demand, consumer price index.

items.q: Which term is described by “the market value of all final goods and services produced within a country in a year”?
o: disposable income
gross national product
gross domestic product
net factor income from abroad
items.s: gross domestic product is the market value of all final goods and services produced within a country in a year.

items.q: The statement “demand for which the percentage change in quantity is smaller than that in price” describes which of the following?
o: inferior good
normal good
elastic demand
inelastic demand
items.s: inelastic demand is demand for which the percentage change in quantity is smaller than that in price.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines structural unemployment?
o: a policy of encouraging local production of goods formerly imported
joblessness caused by a mismatch between workers skills and available jobs
the ratio of the change in national income to the change that caused it
the use of government spending and taxation to influence the economy
items.s: structural unemployment: joblessness caused by a mismatch between workers skills and available jobs. The other options describe fiscal policy, import substitution, multiplier.

items.q: Which of the following best describes demand?
o: the exchange of goods and services between one country and another
the output at which total revenue equals total cost so profit is zero
the quantity of a good buyers are willing and able to buy at each price
a deliberate reduction in the official value of a country currency in terms of other currencies
items.s: demand: the quantity of a good buyers are willing and able to buy at each price. The other options describe break-even point, international trade, devaluation.

items.q: Which of the following best describes disinflation?
o: inflation caused by aggregate demand growing faster than output
a fall in the rate of inflation without a fall in the price level
the process by which banks expand deposits through lending
the addition to total cost from producing one more unit of output
items.s: disinflation: a fall in the rate of inflation without a fall in the price level. The other options describe credit creation, marginal cost, demand pull inflation.

items.q: Which term is described by “the addition to total cost from producing one more unit of output”?
o: economies of scale
fixed cost
break-even point
marginal cost
items.s: marginal cost is the addition to total cost from producing one more unit of output.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines liquidity?
o: the amount by which quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied at a price
the ease with which an asset can be converted into money without loss
anything generally accepted as a medium of exchange and store of value
the responsiveness of demand for one good to a change in the price of another
items.s: liquidity: the ease with which an asset can be converted into money without loss. The other options describe cross elasticity of demand, excess demand, money.

items.q: fixed cost may be defined as
o: the part of the economy that provides services rather than goods
the total quantity of money available in an economy at a time
a cost that does not change with the level of output in the short run
the institution that issues currency and regulates the banking system
items.s: fixed cost: a cost that does not change with the level of output in the short run. The other options describe central bank, tertiary sector, money supply.

items.q: Which term is described by “the ease with which an asset can be converted into money without loss”?
o: money
commercial bank
liquidity
money supply
items.s: liquidity is the ease with which an asset can be converted into money without loss.

items.q: tertiary sector may be defined as
o: the income households have left after paying direct taxes
the addition to total cost from producing one more unit of output
the part of the economy that provides services rather than goods
the loss of competitiveness in other sectors caused by a booming export commodity
items.s: tertiary sector: the part of the economy that provides services rather than goods. The other options describe dutch disease, disposable income, marginal cost.

items.q: Which term is described by “the process by which banks expand deposits through lending”?
o: central bank
liquidity
credit creation
money supply
items.s: credit creation is the process by which banks expand deposits through lending.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines fiscal policy.
o: economic activity that is unrecorded and outside official regulation and taxation
a change in supply caused by a factor other than the price of the good
the condition in which no buyer or seller wishes to trade at another price
the use of government spending and taxation to influence the economy
items.s: fiscal policy: the use of government spending and taxation to influence the economy. The other options describe informal sector, market clearing, shift in supply.

items.q: reserve requirement may be defined as
o: the proportion of deposits that banks must keep as cash or with the central bank
the rate at which a country exports goods in exchange for imports
a fall in the rate of inflation without a fall in the price level
the amount by which government revenue exceeds government spending in a period
items.s: reserve requirement: the proportion of deposits that banks must keep as cash or with the central bank. The other options describe budget surplus, terms of trade, disinflation.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines gross national product.
o: the fall in the value of capital goods used up in production
improvement in income living standards and economic structure of a country
the amount by which quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded at a price
gross domestic product plus net factor income from abroad
items.s: gross national product: gross domestic product plus net factor income from abroad. The other options describe economic development, excess supply, depreciation.

items.q: Which of the following best describes contractionary policy?
o: the buying and selling of government securities by the central bank
the fall in average cost that comes with a larger scale of production
the quantity of a good producers are willing to offer at each price
a policy that reduces aggregate demand through lower spending or higher taxes
items.s: contractionary policy: a policy that reduces aggregate demand through lower spending or higher taxes. The other options describe open market operation, economies of scale, supply.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines disposable income.
o: a deliberate reduction in the official value of a country currency in terms of other currencies
the income households have left after paying direct taxes
the method of measuring GDP by adding consumption investment government spending and net exports
a cost that changes directly with the number of units produced
items.s: disposable income: the income households have left after paying direct taxes. The other options describe variable cost, expenditure approach, devaluation.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines tariff?
o: total cost divided by the number of units produced
a tax imposed on imported goods to raise revenue or protect domestic producers
the condition in which no buyer or seller wishes to trade at another price
the responsiveness of demand for one good to a change in the price of another
items.s: tariff: a tax imposed on imported goods to raise revenue or protect domestic producers. The other options describe average cost, market clearing, cross elasticity of demand.

items.q: break-even point may be defined as
o: the output at which total revenue equals total cost so profit is zero
demand for which the percentage change in quantity is smaller than that in price
inflation caused by aggregate demand growing faster than output
a bank that accepts deposits from the public and creates credit
items.s: break-even point: the output at which total revenue equals total cost so profit is zero. The other options describe inelastic demand, demand pull inflation, commercial bank.

items.q: The statement “a good whose demand falls when household income rises” describes which of the following?
o: normal good
elastic demand
income elasticity of demand
inferior good
items.s: inferior good is a good whose demand falls when household income rises.

items.q: open market operation may be defined as
o: a record of all economic transactions between a country and the rest of the world
the buying and selling of government securities by the central bank
the ratio of the change in national income to the change that caused it
the part of the economy that produces raw materials directly from nature
items.s: open market operation: the buying and selling of government securities by the central bank. The other options describe multiplier, balance of payments, primary sector.

items.q: Which term is described by “price multiplied by the quantity of a good sold”?
o: fixed cost
contribution
total revenue
break-even point
items.s: total revenue is price multiplied by the quantity of a good sold.

items.q: Which term is described by “economic activity that is unrecorded and outside official regulation and taxation”?
o: secondary sector
primary sector
informal sector
import substitution
items.s: informal sector is economic activity that is unrecorded and outside official regulation and taxation.

the responsiveness of demand for one good to a change in the price of another
the ratio of the change in national income to the change that caused it
the output at which total revenue equals total cost so profit is zero
items.s: liquidity: the ease with which an asset can be converted into money without loss. The other options describe cross elasticity of demand, multiplier, break-even point.

o: comparative advantage
international trade
disinflation
balance of payments

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines import substitution.
o: a sustained fall in the general price level of goods and services
a policy of encouraging local production of goods formerly imported
the quantity bought and sold when the market is in equilibrium
the excess of price over average variable cost for each unit sold
items.s: import substitution: a policy of encouraging local production of goods formerly imported. The other options describe equilibrium quantity, deflation, contribution.

items.q: Which term is described by “the amount by which government spending exceeds government revenue in a period”?
o: contractionary policy
fiscal policy
budget deficit
monetary policy
items.s: budget deficit is the amount by which government spending exceeds government revenue in a period.

items.q: Which of the following best describes market clearing?
o: a bank that accepts deposits from the public and creates credit
the condition in which no buyer or seller wishes to trade at another price
the proportion of deposits that banks must keep as cash or with the central bank
demand for which the percentage change in quantity exceeds that in price
items.s: market clearing: the condition in which no buyer or seller wishes to trade at another price. The other options describe reserve requirement, commercial bank, elastic demand.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines consumer price index?
o: the total income earned by the factors of production owned by residents of a country
the situation of people who are willing and able to work but have no job
a measure of the average price of a fixed basket of consumer goods
total cost divided by the number of units produced
items.s: consumer price index: a measure of the average price of a fixed basket of consumer goods. The other options describe unemployment, average cost, national income.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines cross elasticity of demand.
o: a record of all economic transactions between a country and the rest of the world
the responsiveness of demand for one good to a change in the price of another
the total quantity of money available in an economy at a time
the amount by which government revenue exceeds government spending in a period
items.s: cross elasticity of demand: the responsiveness of demand for one good to a change in the price of another. The other options describe budget surplus, balance of payments, money supply.

items.q: Which term is described by “a good whose demand rises when household income rises”?
o: normal good
price elasticity of demand
elastic demand
arc elasticity
items.s: normal good is a good whose demand rises when household income rises.

items.q: contractionary policy may be defined as
o: the market value of all final goods and services produced within a country in a year
the ratio of the change in national income to the change that caused it
a policy that reduces aggregate demand through lower spending or higher taxes
the situation of people who are willing and able to work but have no job
items.s: contractionary policy: a policy that reduces aggregate demand through lower spending or higher taxes. The other options describe gross domestic product, multiplier, unemployment.

items.q: The statement “the condition in which no buyer or seller wishes to trade at another price” describes which of the following?
o: supply
excess supply
equilibrium quantity
market clearing
items.s: market clearing is the condition in which no buyer or seller wishes to trade at another price.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines expenditure approach?
o: the proportion of deposits that banks must keep as cash or with the central bank
the income households have left after paying direct taxes
a sustained fall in the general price level of goods and services
the method of measuring GDP by adding consumption investment government spending and net exports
items.s: expenditure approach: the method of measuring GDP by adding consumption investment government spending and net exports. The other options describe reserve requirement, deflation, disposable income.

items.q: Which of the following best describes national income?
o: elasticity measured between two points using their average values
the rate at which a country exports goods in exchange for imports
the total income earned by the factors of production owned by residents of a country
gross national product less depreciation of capital
items.s: national income: the total income earned by the factors of production owned by residents of a country. The other options describe terms of trade, net national product, arc elasticity.

items.q: The statement “the excess of price over average variable cost for each unit sold” describes which of the following?
o: average cost
contribution
fixed cost
economies of scale
items.s: contribution is the excess of price over average variable cost for each unit sold.

items.q: The statement “gross domestic product plus net factor income from abroad” describes which of the following?
o: net national product
gross domestic product
disposable income
gross national product
items.s: gross national product is gross domestic product plus net factor income from abroad.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines primary sector?
o: the output at which total revenue equals total cost so profit is zero
the buying and selling of government securities by the central bank
the process by which banks expand deposits through lending
the part of the economy that produces raw materials directly from nature
items.s: primary sector: the part of the economy that produces raw materials directly from nature. The other options describe break-even point, credit creation, open market operation.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines arc elasticity.
o: a policy that increases aggregate demand through higher spending or lower taxes
the output at which total revenue equals total cost so profit is zero
elasticity measured between two points using their average values
the addition to total cost from producing one more unit of output
items.s: arc elasticity: elasticity measured between two points using their average values. The other options describe marginal cost, expansionary policy, break-even point.

items.q: Which term is described by “the rate at which a country exports goods in exchange for imports”?
o: terms of trade
tariff
balance of payments
international trade
items.s: terms of trade is the rate at which a country exports goods in exchange for imports.

items.q: Which term is described by “the responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in the price of the good”?
o: price elasticity of demand
inelastic demand
arc elasticity
elastic demand
items.s: price elasticity of demand is the responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in the price of the good.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines comparative advantage.
o: price multiplied by the quantity of a good sold
the condition in which no buyer or seller wishes to trade at another price
the ability of a country to produce a good at a lower opportunity cost than another
the output at which total revenue equals total cost so profit is zero
items.s: comparative advantage: the ability of a country to produce a good at a lower opportunity cost than another. The other options describe market clearing, total revenue, break-even point.

items.q: The statement “the addition to total cost from producing one more unit of output” describes which of the following?
o: variable cost
contribution
marginal cost
average cost
items.s: marginal cost is the addition to total cost from producing one more unit of output.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines deflation?
o: the quantity of a good buyers are willing and able to buy at each price
a sustained fall in the general price level of goods and services
the method of measuring GDP by adding consumption investment government spending and net exports
investment by a firm in productive assets located in another country
items.s: deflation: a sustained fall in the general price level of goods and services. The other options describe foreign direct investment, demand, expenditure approach.

items.q: Which term is described by “the fall in the value of capital goods used up in production”?
o: depreciation
expenditure approach
gross domestic product
gross national product
items.s: depreciation is the fall in the value of capital goods used up in production.

items.q: Which term is described by “total cost divided by the number of units produced”?
o: average cost
break-even point
total revenue
contribution
items.s: average cost is total cost divided by the number of units produced.

items.q: The statement “the total income earned by the factors of production owned by residents of a country” describes which of the following?
o: net national product
expenditure approach
national income
net factor income from abroad
items.s: national income is the total income earned by the factors of production owned by residents of a country.

items.q: equilibrium quantity may be defined as
o: demand for which the percentage change in quantity exceeds that in price
the part of the economy that produces raw materials directly from nature
the quantity bought and sold when the market is in equilibrium
a policy that reduces aggregate demand through lower spending or higher taxes
items.s: equilibrium quantity: the quantity bought and sold when the market is in equilibrium. The other options describe primary sector, contractionary policy, elastic demand.

items.q: The statement “the use of government spending and taxation to influence the economy” describes which of the following?
o: fiscal policy
monetary policy
multiplier
open market operation
items.s: fiscal policy is the use of government spending and taxation to influence the economy.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines break-even point.
o: gross domestic product plus net factor income from abroad
a measure of the average price of a fixed basket of consumer goods
the responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in household income
the output at which total revenue equals total cost so profit is zero
items.s: break-even point: the output at which total revenue equals total cost so profit is zero. The other options describe income elasticity of demand, gross national product, consumer price index.

items.q: Which term is described by “the use of government spending and taxation to influence the economy”?
o: multiplier
expansionary policy
fiscal policy
monetary policy
items.s: fiscal policy is the use of government spending and taxation to influence the economy.

items.q: The statement “the price at which quantity demanded equals quantity supplied” describes which of the following?
o: equilibrium price
supply
equilibrium quantity
demand
items.s: equilibrium price is the price at which quantity demanded equals quantity supplied.

items.q: Which term is described by “a good whose demand falls when household income rises”?
o: elastic demand
price elasticity of demand
inferior good
cross elasticity of demand
items.s: inferior good is a good whose demand falls when household income rises.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines income elasticity of demand?
o: the process by which banks expand deposits through lending
the responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in household income
the income households have left after paying direct taxes
a policy of encouraging local production of goods formerly imported
items.s: income elasticity of demand: the responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in household income. The other options describe credit creation, disposable income, import substitution.

items.q: The statement “a policy of encouraging local production of goods formerly imported” describes which of the following?
o: import substitution
informal sector
dutch disease
tertiary sector
items.s: import substitution is a policy of encouraging local production of goods formerly imported.

items.q: An economy has a marginal propensity to consume of 0.5. Investment spending rises by 100 million naira. Find the resulting change in national income in million naira.
items.s: Multiplier = 1/(1 - 0.5) = 2, so change in income = 2 x 100 = 200 million naira.

items.q: Nominal GDP in a year is 720 billion naira and the GDP deflator for that year is 160. Find real GDP in base year prices, in billion naira.
items.s: Real GDP = (nominal GDP / deflator) x 100 = (720 / 160) x 100 = 450 billion naira.

items.q: With its given resources a country can produce either 400 units of good X or 2500 units of good Y, using all its resources in each case. Find the opportunity cost of one unit of X in terms of Y.
items.s: Opportunity cost of one X = units of Y given up / units of X gained = 2500 / 400 = 6.25 units of Y.

items.q: A firm has fixed cost of 60000 naira, sells its product at 400 naira per unit and has an average variable cost of 120 naira per unit. Find the break-even quantity in units.
items.s: Break-even quantity = FC / (price - AVC) = 60000 / (400 - 120) = 214.29 units.

items.q: The demand and supply functions are Qd = 440 - 2P and Qs = 80 + 6P. At a price of 22 naira, find the size of the excess demand.
items.s: At P = 22: Qd = 396 and Qs = 212, so excess demand = 396 - 212 = 184 units.

items.q: The price of a good rises from 30 naira to 60 naira and quantity demanded falls from 800 units to 600 units. Find the price elasticity of demand, ignoring the negative sign.
items.s: Elasticity = (% change in quantity) / (% change in price) = (-200/800) / (30/30) = 0.25.

items.q: When the price of a good falls from 30 naira to 20 naira, quantity demanded rises from 300 units to 350 units. Find the arc elasticity of demand, ignoring the negative sign.
items.s: Arc elasticity = ((Q2 - Q1)/average Q) / ((P2 - P1)/average P) = (50/325) / (10/25) = 0.385.

items.q: Household income rises from 30000 naira to 36000 naira and the quantity of a good demanded rises from 300 units to 330 units. Find the income elasticity of demand.
items.s: Income elasticity = (% change in quantity) / (% change in income) = (30/300) / (6000/30000) = 0.5.

items.q: In an economy the marginal propensity to consume is 0.4. Find the value of the investment multiplier.

An economy records consumption of 800 billion naira, investment of 300 billion naira, government spending of 140 billion naira, exports of 120 billion naira and imports of 110 billion naira. Find GDP by the expenditure approach, in billion naira.

A country has a GDP of 900 billion naira, net factor income from abroad of 40 billion naira, depreciation of 120 billion naira and indirect taxes of 50 billion naira. Find national income at factor cost, in billion naira.
items.s: GNP = 900 + 40 = 940, NNP = 940 - 120 = 820, and national income = 820 - 50 = 770 billion naira.

items.q: The consumer price index of a country rises from 160 in one year to 179 in the next year. Find the rate of inflation, in per cent.
items.s: Inflation rate = ((CPI2 - CPI1)/CPI1) x 100 = ((179 - 160)/160) x 100 = 11.88 per cent.

items.q: A firm's total cost function is TC = 300 + 20Q + 2Q^2. Find the marginal cost when output is 10 units, taking marginal cost as the derivative of total cost.
items.s: MC = dTC/dQ = 20 + 4Q = 20 + 4 x 10 = 60 naira.

items.q: A firm's total cost function is TC = 1500 + 10Q. Find the average cost when output is 60 units.
items.s: TC = 1500 + 10 x 60 = 2100, so AC = TC/Q = 2100 / 60 = 35 naira per unit.

items.q: A unit tax of 60 naira is imposed on a good. The price elasticity of demand is 5 and the price elasticity of supply is 2. Find the part of the tax per unit that is borne by consumers, in naira.
items.s: Consumer share = tax x Es / (Ed + Es) = 60 x 2 / (5 + 2) = 17.14 naira.

items.q: The demand curve for a good is P = 150 - 2Q and the market price is 75 naira. Find the consumer surplus.
items.s: At P = 75, Q = (150 - 75)/2 = 37.5, so consumer surplus = half x 37.5 x 75 = 1406.25.

items.q: The supply curve for a good is P = 50 + 2Q and the market price is 100 naira. Find the producer surplus.
items.s: At P = 100, Q = (100 - 50)/2 = 25, so producer surplus = half x 25 x 50 = 625.

items.s: Multiplier = 1/(1 - 0.8) = 5, so change in income = 5 x 500 = 2500 million naira.

items.q: Nominal GDP in a year is 720 billion naira and the GDP deflator for that year is 120. Find real GDP in base year prices, in billion naira.

items.s: Arc elasticity = ((Q2 - Q1)/average Q) / ((P2 - P1)/average P) = (20/210) / (20/70) = 0.333.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “total cost divided by the number of units produced”
o: total revenue
average cost
fixed cost
break-even point
items.s: average cost is total cost divided by the number of units produced.

items.q: deflation is best described as
o: the situation of people who are willing and able to work but have no job
a sustained fall in the general price level of goods and services
a fall in the rate of inflation without a fall in the price level
inflation caused by aggregate demand growing faster than output
items.s: deflation: a sustained fall in the general price level of goods and services. The other options describe demand pull inflation, unemployment, disinflation.

items.q: The best definition of depreciation among these is
o: the method of measuring GDP by adding consumption investment government spending and net exports
the fall in the value of capital goods used up in production
the total income earned by the factors of production owned by residents of a country
gross national product less depreciation of capital
items.s: depreciation: the fall in the value of capital goods used up in production. The other options describe net national product, expenditure approach, national income.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what unemployment means.
o: the situation of people who are willing and able to work but have no job
a fall in the rate of inflation without a fall in the price level
inflation caused by rising costs of production being passed on as higher prices
a measure of the average price of a fixed basket of consumer goods
items.s: unemployment: the situation of people who are willing and able to work but have no job. The other options describe disinflation, cost push inflation, consumer price index.

items.q: Which of the following does NOT belong to Demand, supply and market equilibrium?
o: equilibrium price
supply
open market operation
demand
items.s: Every other option belongs to Demand, supply and market equilibrium. “open market operation” belongs to Fiscal and monetary policy, not Demand, supply and market equilibrium.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the amount by which government spending exceeds government revenue in a period”
o: expansionary policy
open market operation
multiplier
budget deficit
items.s: budget deficit is the amount by which government spending exceeds government revenue in a period.

items.q: In this course, variable cost refers to
o: a cost that does not change with the level of output in the short run
a cost that changes directly with the number of units produced
the output at which total revenue equals total cost so profit is zero
the addition to total cost from producing one more unit of output
items.s: variable cost: a cost that changes directly with the number of units produced. The other options describe marginal cost, break-even point, fixed cost.

items.q: The best definition of commercial bank among these is
o: the proportion of deposits that banks must keep as cash or with the central bank
anything generally accepted as a medium of exchange and store of value
a bank that accepts deposits from the public and creates credit
the process by which banks expand deposits through lending
items.s: commercial bank: a bank that accepts deposits from the public and creates credit. The other options describe reserve requirement, credit creation, money.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a policy of encouraging local production of goods formerly imported”
o: informal sector
import substitution
secondary sector
primary sector
items.s: import substitution is a policy of encouraging local production of goods formerly imported.

items.q: The best definition of primary sector among these is
o: an economy that depends heavily on a single commodity for its revenue
the part of the economy that produces raw materials directly from nature
the part of the economy that provides services rather than goods
the loss of competitiveness in other sectors caused by a booming export commodity
items.s: primary sector: the part of the economy that produces raw materials directly from nature. The other options describe monoculture economy, tertiary sector, dutch disease.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a good whose demand falls when household income rises”
o: income elasticity of demand
normal good
inelastic demand
inferior good
items.s: inferior good is a good whose demand falls when household income rises.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what terms of trade means.
o: the ability of a country to produce a good at a lower opportunity cost than another
investment by a firm in productive assets located in another country
the exchange of goods and services between one country and another
the rate at which a country exports goods in exchange for imports
items.s: terms of trade: the rate at which a country exports goods in exchange for imports. The other options describe international trade, foreign direct investment, comparative advantage.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the loss of competitiveness in other sectors caused by a booming export commodity”
o: monoculture economy
dutch disease
primary sector
import substitution
items.s: dutch disease is the loss of competitiveness in other sectors caused by a booming export commodity.

items.q: The statement “the situation of people who are willing and able to work but have no job” describes which of the following?
o: disinflation
unemployment
consumer price index
deflation
items.s: unemployment is the situation of people who are willing and able to work but have no job.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what contribution means.
o: the fall in average cost that comes with a larger scale of production
the output at which total revenue equals total cost so profit is zero
a cost that does not change with the level of output in the short run

items.q: A firm's total cost function is TC = 1200 + 15Q. Find the average cost when output is 80 units.
items.s: TC = 1200 + 15 x 80 = 2400, so AC = TC/Q = 2400 / 80 = 30 naira per unit.

items.q: A firm has fixed cost of 60000 naira, sells its product at 300 naira per unit and has an average variable cost of 80 naira per unit. Find the break-even quantity in units.
items.s: Break-even quantity = FC / (price - AVC) = 60000 / (300 - 80) = 272.73 units.

items.q: A unit tax of 20 naira is imposed on a good. The price elasticity of demand is 1 and the price elasticity of supply is 2. Find the part of the tax per unit that is borne by consumers, in naira.
items.s: Consumer share = tax x Es / (Ed + Es) = 20 x 2 / (1 + 2) = 13.33 naira.

items.q: The supply curve for a good is P = 40 + 4Q and the market price is 140 naira. Find the producer surplus.
items.s: At P = 140, Q = (140 - 40)/4 = 25, so producer surplus = half x 25 x 100 = 1250.

items.q: Household income rises from 25000 naira to 37500 naira and the quantity of a good demanded rises from 100 units to 160 units. Find the income elasticity of demand.
items.s: Income elasticity = (% change in quantity) / (% change in income) = (60/100) / (12500/25000) = 1.2.

items.q: A country has a GDP of 900 billion naira, net factor income from abroad of 80 billion naira, depreciation of 80 billion naira and indirect taxes of 40 billion naira. Find national income at factor cost, in billion naira.
items.s: GNP = 900 + 80 = 980, NNP = 980 - 80 = 900, and national income = 900 - 40 = 860 billion naira.

items.q: A firm's total cost function is TC = 300 + 25Q + 4Q^2. Find the marginal cost when output is 5 units, taking marginal cost as the derivative of total cost.
items.s: MC = dTC/dQ = 25 + 8Q = 25 + 8 x 5 = 65 naira.

items.q: The demand curve for a good is P = 80 - 5Q and the market price is 16 naira. Find the consumer surplus.
items.s: At P = 16, Q = (80 - 16)/5 = 12.8, so consumer surplus = half x 12.8 x 64 = 409.6.

items.q: For a certain good Qd = 260 - 2P and Qs = 80 + 4P. Find the equilibrium quantity.
items.s: Equilibrium price = (260 - 80)/(2 + 4) = 30, so Q = 80 + 4 x 30 = 200 units.

items.q: The demand and supply functions are Qd = 400 - 4P and Qs = 100 + 2P. At a price of 35 naira, find the size of the excess demand.
items.s: At P = 35: Qd = 260 and Qs = 170, so excess demand = 260 - 170 = 90 units.

items.q: The price of a good rises from 25 naira to 31 naira and quantity demanded falls from 1000 units to 600 units. Find the price elasticity of demand, ignoring the negative sign.
items.s: Elasticity = (% change in quantity) / (% change in price) = (-400/1000) / (6/25) = 1.67.

items.q: An economy has a marginal propensity to consume of 0.9. Investment spending rises by 500 million naira. Find the resulting change in national income in million naira.
items.s: Multiplier = 1/(1 - 0.9) = 10, so change in income = 10 x 500 = 5000 million naira.

expenditure approach

joblessness caused by a mismatch between workers skills and available jobs

the quantity of a good buyers are willing and able to buy at each price

a change in supply caused by a factor other than the price of the good

price multiplied by the quantity of a good sold

gross national product
gross domestic product
net national product

a measure of the average price of a fixed basket of consumer goods
inflation caused by rising costs of production being passed on as higher prices

a cost that does not change with the level of output in the short run

the total income earned by the factors of production owned by residents of a country

dutch disease
import substitution

consumer price index
demand pull inflation

budget surplus

fiscal policy

o: contractionary policy

open market operation

demand pull inflation
items.s: unemployment is the situation of people who are willing and able to work but have no job.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains budget surplus.
o: the buying and selling of government securities by the central bank
the amount by which government revenue exceeds government spending in a period
a policy that increases aggregate demand through higher spending or lower taxes
the use of government spending and taxation to influence the economy
items.s: budget surplus: the amount by which government revenue exceeds government spending in a period. The other options describe expansionary policy, open market operation, fiscal policy.

items.q: “the excess of price over average variable cost for each unit sold” is the definition of
o: economies of scale
total revenue
contribution
average cost
items.s: contribution is the excess of price over average variable cost for each unit sold.

items.q: “the part of the economy that produces raw materials directly from nature” is the definition of
o: secondary sector
primary sector
tertiary sector
import substitution
items.s: primary sector is the part of the economy that produces raw materials directly from nature.

items.q: “total cost divided by the number of units produced” is the definition of
o: average cost
variable cost
economies of scale
marginal cost
items.s: average cost is total cost divided by the number of units produced.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains deflation.
o: the situation of people who are willing and able to work but have no job
joblessness caused by a mismatch between workers skills and available jobs
a sustained rise in the general price level of goods and services
a sustained fall in the general price level of goods and services
items.s: deflation: a sustained fall in the general price level of goods and services. The other options describe unemployment, structural unemployment, inflation.

items.q: balance of payments may be defined as
o: a record of all economic transactions between a country and the rest of the world
the exchange of goods and services between one country and another
the rate at which a country exports goods in exchange for imports
improvement in income living standards and economic structure of a country
items.s: balance of payments: a record of all economic transactions between a country and the rest of the world. The other options describe terms of trade, economic development, international trade.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains money.
o: the process by which banks expand deposits through lending
anything generally accepted as a medium of exchange and store of value
a bank that accepts deposits from the public and creates credit
the ease with which an asset can be converted into money without loss
items.s: money: anything generally accepted as a medium of exchange and store of value. The other options describe commercial bank, credit creation, liquidity.

items.q: The correct meaning of commercial bank is
o: the total quantity of money available in an economy at a time
anything generally accepted as a medium of exchange and store of value
the ease with which an asset can be converted into money without loss
a bank that accepts deposits from the public and creates credit
items.s: commercial bank: a bank that accepts deposits from the public and creates credit. The other options describe money, money supply, liquidity.

items.q: The correct meaning of tariff is
o: a deliberate reduction in the official value of a country currency in terms of other currencies
the rate at which a country exports goods in exchange for imports
the exchange of goods and services between one country and another
a tax imposed on imported goods to raise revenue or protect domestic producers
items.s: tariff: a tax imposed on imported goods to raise revenue or protect domestic producers. The other options describe devaluation, terms of trade, international trade.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains budget deficit.
o: the ratio of the change in national income to the change that caused it
the use of money supply and interest rates by the central bank to influence the economy
the amount by which government spending exceeds government revenue in a period
the amount by which government revenue exceeds government spending in a period
items.s: budget deficit: the amount by which government spending exceeds government revenue in a period. The other options describe budget surplus, multiplier, monetary policy.

items.q: In this course, dutch disease refers to
o: the loss of competitiveness in other sectors caused by a booming export commodity
economic activity that is unrecorded and outside official regulation and taxation
the part of the economy that produces raw materials directly from nature
the part of the economy that transforms raw materials into manufactured goods
items.s: dutch disease: the loss of competitiveness in other sectors caused by a booming export commodity. The other options describe secondary sector, primary sector, informal sector.

items.q: In this course, reserve requirement refers to
o: the process by which banks expand deposits through lending
a bank that accepts deposits from the public and creates credit
the ease with which an asset can be converted into money without loss
the proportion of deposits that banks must keep as cash or with the central bank
items.s: reserve requirement: the proportion of deposits that banks must keep as cash or with the central bank. The other options describe credit creation, commercial bank, liquidity.

items.q: In this course, total revenue refers to
o: a cost that changes directly with the number of units produced
price multiplied by the quantity of a good sold
the fall in average cost that comes with a larger scale of production
total cost divided by the number of units produced
items.s: total revenue: price multiplied by the quantity of a good sold. The other options describe variable cost, average cost, economies of scale.

items.q: “the responsiveness of demand for one good to a change in the price of another” is the definition of
o: income elasticity of demand
normal good
cross elasticity of demand
inferior good
items.s: cross elasticity of demand is the responsiveness of demand for one good to a change in the price of another.

items.q: gross domestic product may be defined as
o: the total income earned by the factors of production owned by residents of a country
the income households have left after paying direct taxes
gross national product less depreciation of capital
the market value of all final goods and services produced within a country in a year
items.s: gross domestic product: the market value of all final goods and services produced within a country in a year. The other options describe net national product, disposable income, national income.

items.q: The correct meaning of reserve requirement is
o: the institution that issues currency and regulates the banking system
a bank that accepts deposits from the public and creates credit
the process by which banks expand deposits through lending
the proportion of deposits that banks must keep as cash or with the central bank
items.s: reserve requirement: the proportion of deposits that banks must keep as cash or with the central bank. The other options describe commercial bank, central bank, credit creation.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains net factor income from abroad.
o: the difference between income earned abroad and income paid abroad
the method of measuring GDP by adding consumption investment government spending and net exports
the fall in the value of capital goods used up in production
the total income earned by the factors of production owned by residents of a country
items.s: net factor income from abroad: the difference between income earned abroad and income paid abroad. The other options describe depreciation, expenditure approach, national income.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains average cost.
o: the addition to total cost from producing one more unit of output
the output at which total revenue equals total cost so profit is zero
total cost divided by the number of units produced
price multiplied by the quantity of a good sold
items.s: average cost: total cost divided by the number of units produced. The other options describe marginal cost, total revenue, break-even point.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains net national product.
o: the market value of all final goods and services produced within a country in a year
gross national product less depreciation of capital
the difference between income earned abroad and income paid abroad
the income households have left after paying direct taxes
items.s: net national product: gross national product less depreciation of capital. The other options describe net factor income from abroad, disposable income, gross domestic product.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a change in supply caused by a factor other than the price of the good”
o: equilibrium quantity
supply
equilibrium price
shift in supply
items.s: shift in supply is a change in supply caused by a factor other than the price of the good.

items.q: “gross domestic product plus net factor income from abroad” is the definition of
o: national income
depreciation
gross national product
net factor income from abroad
items.s: gross national product is gross domestic product plus net factor income from abroad.
